title: How is a remittance applied to Bills of Lading and Transport Documents fees?
content:
## Scope

This Bills of Lading and Transport Documents policy governs how a customer's remittance is applied to the documentation fees of a transport document, such as issuance, correction, release, switch and reissue fees.

## Formal clauses

1. A remittance is applied to one document's fees, written with the remittance reference exactly as quoted and with the amount remitted.
2. The amount applied may not exceed the document's documentation charges due; the amount booked is the lower of the amount remitted and the charges due, and any excess is returned by finance and not booked.
3. A remittance reference is recorded only once per document.
4. Documentation fees are separate from the booking's freight: a payment made against the booking never settles documentation fees, and a payment against documentation fees never settles freight.

## Worked examples (hypothetical amounts)

| Documentation charges due on the document | Amount remitted | Amount booked on the document | Excess |
|---|---|---|---|
| USD 140.00 | USD 90.00 | USD 90.00 | none |
| USD 140.00 | USD 140.00 | USD 140.00 | none |
| USD 140.00 | USD 200.00 | USD 140.00 | USD 60.00, returned by finance, not booked |

## Points of judgement

- **The same remittance reference is quoted again for the same document.** It is not recorded a second time.
- **The customer has paid its freight on the booking and believes its documentation fees are covered.** They are not; the two balances are separate.
- **Which reference is written?** The remittance reference exactly as the customer quotes it.
